questions.stem: At 3:00, the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock is:
questions.explanation: Hour hand at 3 (90° from 12, clockwise); minute hand at 12 (0°). Difference = 90°. General formula — angle between the two hands = |30 × H − 5.5 × M|, where H = hours, M = minutes. At 3:00 → |30 × 3 − 5.5 × 0| = 90°. Classic benchmark angles: 12:00 = 0°; 3:00 = 90°; 6:00 = 180°; 9:00 = 270° (or equivalently 90° the other way).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: At 4:20, the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand is:
questions.explanation: Formula |30 × 4 − 5.5 × 20| = |120 − 110| = 10°. The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute (30° per hour ÷ 60 min), so at 4:20 it is 0.5 × 20 = 10° past the 4 mark (at 120 + 10 = 130°). The minute hand is at 20 × 6 = 120°. Difference 130 − 120 = 10°.

questions.stem: The hour and minute hands of a clock coincide (overlap) how many times in a 12-hour period?
questions.explanation: In 12 hours, the two hands coincide 11 times — because the minute hand laps the hour hand 11 times. The first coincidence is at 12:00, the last before the next 12:00 is around 11:59-something. Each coincidence happens roughly every 12/11 hours ≈ 65.45 minutes. In 24 hours the hands coincide 22 times.

questions.stem: A clock gains 10 seconds every hour. In a 24-hour period, how much time does it gain?
questions.explanation: 10 seconds/hour × 24 hours = 240 seconds = 4 minutes. Gain-rate questions are direct multiplication once you identify the rate. If a clock loses 5 minutes per day, in a week it loses 35 minutes. If the time is right at 12 noon but it has gained 4 minutes by next noon, the clock now reads 12:04 at true 12:00.

questions.stem: The mirror image of a clock showing 2:30 is:
questions.explanation: Mirror-time formula — Mirror time = 11:60 − given time (when the given time is after 1:00). At 2:30 → 11:60 − 2:30 = 9:30. Verify: the clock shows 2 and 6 positions; reflected across the vertical (12-6 axis), 2 maps to 10, 6 stays at 6 — but the HOUR hand of 2:30 is halfway between 2 and 3; its mirror lies halfway between 9 and 10, which is 9:30.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: In 60 minutes, the minute hand of a clock moves through an angle of:
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes one full revolution (360°) per hour. Therefore it moves 360°/60 = 6° per minute. The hour hand completes 360° in 12 hours — 30° per hour or 0.5° per minute. These two rates are the basis of every clock-angle formula in this topic.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A clock shows 6:15. The angle between the two hands is:
questions.explanation: |30 × 6 − 5.5 × 15| = |180 − 82.5| = 97.5°. Verify: minute hand at 15 → 90°. Hour hand at 6:15 → 180 + 0.5 × 15 = 187.5°. Difference 187.5 − 90 = 97.5°. The 5.5 in the formula comes from the fact that every minute, the minute hand gains 5.5° on the hour hand (6° − 0.5°).
